carte_vide: Empty card? Reload the page (Ctrl+F5): the card comes with the Vision integration and loads by itself.
message_aide:
A real notification, on the computer as on the phone, signed “{produit}” and kept in the notification centre. If a device is off, it waits and expires after a quarter of an hour.

The recipient can be **all devices**, a **category** (every device that has it), or one specific device. These are **Home Assistant labels** — the same ones as for a plug: add them in the card's *Labels* field, or from the device page.
message_automatisation_titre: Sending a message from an automation
message_sans_cible: Without `pc` or `tag`, the message goes to everyone. Each device also has its own `notify` entity, which Home Assistant labels can target.
installation_aide:
The device shows up here by itself, **allowed and without time slots**: link it to a profile with the “User” selector (the choice made in the app is only a suggestion), then add its time slots.

**Updates**: Home Assistant hosts the agent and the app. When a new version arrives with the integration, each device updates by itself — or with the *Install* button on the “Agent version” line if you'd rather stay in control. A PC still on **1.0.0** can't do this yet: run the installer once more on that machine, it will keep its identity and its time slots.

To remove a device, the **Remove a device** section next to this is enough — the agent uninstalls itself. If the machine should never talk to Home Assistant again, you can also run this on it:
courbe_aide: The total number of attempts to reach a blocked site, per machine. Nothing is notified anywhere: a blocked site is simply unreachable. This is where you can read it.
securite_liste_noire_aide:
Two protections that work together, and that don't replace your rules.

The **blocklist** is downloaded from public sources (malware, phishing), at the pace chosen above. Vision knows all its domains, so it can warn you, and blocks part of them through the `hosts` file. The date of the last update is in *Known domains*: “automatic” means nothing until you can see whether it worked.

The **DNS filter** handles the rest: millions of domains, set on the network adapters of each device. It only works because Vision already turns off encrypted DNS in browsers.

⚠️ A blocked site says nothing on the device: no explanation page, no notification. It is simply unreachable. The attempt shows up **here**, with its date.
securite_et_autres: … and {nombre} more. Type part of a name above to search.
securite_avis_aide:
**Popularity** is the worldwide ranking of the most visited sites. **Popular doesn't mean suitable**: adult sites are among the most visited in the world. What it brings is the opposite: a domain nobody visits, contacted by a program you don't know, finally stands out among two hundred other lines. Nothing is blocked because of it: it's a column, not a rule.

**VirusTotal** answers about *programs*: a signature proves that a publisher put its certificate on the line, not that it is honest.

What gets sent is the file's **fingerprint**, never the file. But a fingerprint still tells a third party *which programs run here*: that's the price, and it's better to decide it than to suffer it. Nothing is sent while the switch is off.

The free tier allows four requests per minute: Vision waits its turn and looks first at what isn't signed.
inscrire_aide: Almost everything arrives by itself: what a machine sees joins the list at the next check-in. Only add here what you want to decide **before** it arrives.
portes_aide:
Here the decision is made machine by machine again, and it overrides the one made for all devices — except for a name **banned for everyone**, which nothing reopens.

**Spare an address** targets one precise place inside a blocked site and keeps it open. **Let through** reopens the whole site for the chosen time, then closes it again by itself.

**Opened by** says which program was caught talking to this site — often the browser, and then it doesn't matter; sometimes a program you don't know, and that's when it counts. **Block this program** cuts the source rather than the leak, for all devices.
portes_aucune: no door open on this device
listes_aide:
**The shared decision comes first, and it's final.** What is *blocked* for everyone is closed everywhere: no permission set on a machine, no category, no pass reopens it. It's the only irreversible decision — that's what gives it its meaning.

**The PC decides next, and the strictest rule wins.** *Allowed* means *accepted by default*, not *untouchable*: YouTube can be allowed for everyone and blocked on one PC during school time. A category blocked on the machine, or a time slot in progress, therefore closes an allowed site.

Categories are Home Assistant labels (**Settings → Areas, labels & zones**): same list, same colours. A category applies to sites and programs alike — blocking “Videos” closes both at once.
processus_aide:
Every ten minutes the agent lists what runs on the device, what starts with Windows, scheduled tasks and services that aren't from Microsoft. A classifier suggests a verdict; **nothing changes on a PC until a {decideur} has approved it**.

- **Keep**: we leave it alone.
- **Out of startup**: the program no longer starts by itself, but still starts when you launch it. This is what we do to game launchers and keyboard or mouse utilities.
- **Harmful**: the process is stopped whenever it shows up.
- **Uninstall** 🗑: the program is removed from the device. The button only appears if “Uninstall by the agent” is on, it is decided one program at a time, and it asks for confirmation: **it can't be undone**. The agent runs the program's official uninstaller, silently, and reports here whether it worked. When a program has no known silent uninstall, the agent doesn't try anything and answers “to remove by hand”. Windows, Microsoft programs, drivers, game anti-cheat and the Vision agent are never uninstalled this way.

A game's anti-cheat (Vanguard, BattlEye, Denuvo) is never touched: it must start with Windows, otherwise the game refuses to launch.

“↺” puts an item back to sort and **has the agent restore** what it had changed.
veille_aide: The theme, the music or radio and night mode are set on each device (Vision → Settings): every TV, every phone has its own. Here, you only choose the dashboards and cards that are made available.
retrait_aide:
A device is removed from its person's page (the “Today” tab, then the person): **Remove…**, under the device. Vision shows what will be lost and asks you to type the device's name to confirm.

Its agent learns about it at the next contact: it frees the machine — `hosts` file, DNS, probe — confirms, then deletes itself. Nothing to do on the spot.

⚠️ This also deletes its time slots, its rules and its history. A device that is off keeps the instruction for three months: it will uninstall itself the next time it starts.
pause_generale_en_cours: **Everything is blocked until {heure}**: protected devices stay blocked until then. “Allow again” ends it sooner.
pause_generale_aucune: Nothing is blocked all at once right now. “Block everything” blocks all protected devices for 30 minutes, after confirmation.
pause_generale_confirmation: Block everything: all protected devices will be blocked for 30 minutes. Continue?
